messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: derived parameter defs & I/O
parts:
As things stand, when you write derived parameters,
the code in the derived parameter block is run,
but NOT the code in the model. Thus if the transforms
are defined in the model, they won't be part of the
output -- the variables will remain zero.

Here's the plan of how things should go. I could
change this so that the model statements (other than
samples) are also run before output of derived params.

What you need to do is move the derived param definitions
into a block after the declarations. For example,

WRONG:

...
derived parameters {
double z_sq; // declared as derived param
...
}
model {
z_sq <- z * z; // WRONG: defined in model
...
}

RIGHT:

derived parameters {
double z_sq;
...
z_sq <- z * z; // OK: defined in derived param block
}
model {
...
}

I plan to add some error checking that will actually
make the WRONG line a compile error. I need to do
this in general so that

* assignments in derived data only to derived data
variables

* assignments in derived params only to derived param vars

* assignments in derived quantities only to derived quants

I've added truly local variables, too. So if you want to,
you can do this in a model

model {
...
for (n in 1:N) {
double mu; // local var declared at head of statement block
mu <- alpha * x[n] + beta; // assigned within block scope
y[n] ~ normal(mu,sigma);
}
...
}

* local vars can be assigned only within the block of statements
in which they were defined

There is already error handling in place for this.

Now I could change this behavior so that the model
code is run again (I set up the generator so I can
drop the sampling statements, which won't need to be
run).

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: derived parameter defs & I/O
parts:
Local vars probably don't work yet. It shouldn't
take long to get the code generated.

Backward compatibility with people's programming
idioms is hard and not necessarily desirable.

I'm hoping that sensible error messages will go
a long way to mitigating the transition problems.

I think the main problem with the Wawro model is
that I changed the Stan language after we built
the first version! (Though I wasn't actually planning
to allow the derived parameters to be monitored --
I always thought of them as locals -- the params are
what goes into HMC and actually gets sampled -- but
then there's code duplication issues recreating them
on the outside ...)

The plan is to store all the parameters and
derived parameters. The only issue is that the
derived parameter transforms need to be defined in
the derived parameter block rather than in the model.

I was thinking of a "local" or "nuisance" label for
param declarations which would prevent their being
written. But I decided it'd be better to just have
a convention of writing all params, derived params
and derived quantities. Those that a user doesn't
want to write can be declared as local. There's
no such thing as a local parameter, though -- they
always all get written --- they're what's getting
sampled in HMC/NUTS and we need to monitor convergence.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: derived parameter defs & I/O
parts:
I just want to mention that at least in some bugs examples, 
I guess storing the derived parameters is not necessary. 
In some cases, it is convenient to declare an array of 
parameters, and use the loop from 1 to N in the model 
declaration.  So I have ended up using something like this

parameters {
   int N;
   double alpha[N-1];
}

derived parameters {
  double yaalpha[N];
  yaalpha[1] <- 0;
  for (i in 2:N) yaalpha[i] <- alpha[i - 1];
}

In this case, monitoring yaalpha[1] can be problematic. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: derived parameter defs & I/O
parts:
On 1/5/12 2:32 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> I just want to mention that at least in some bugs examples,
> I guess storing the derived parameters is not necessary.

If a parameter doesn't need to be stored, it can
be moved from being a derived parameter to being
a local parameter in the model without changing the
behavior of the model.

> In some cases, it is convenient to declare an array of
> parameters, and use the loop from 1 to N in the model
> declaration. So I have ended up using something like this
>
> parameters {
> int N;
> double alpha[N-1];
> }
>
> derived parameters {
> double yaalpha[N];
> yaalpha[1] <- 0;
> for (i in 2:N) yaalpha[i] <- alpha[i - 1];
> }
>
> In this case, monitoring yaalpha[1] can be problematic.

The issue here's the semantics of "monitor",
which really involves two things:

1. save/write: we'll do this for all parameters
and derived parameters.

2. convergence monitor: we'll do this for all
parameters.

It would be convenient for external convergence monitoring
to also write the unconstrained version of the parameter
vector as seen by HMC. The parameter view to clients is
the constrained version (e.g., deviations are positive,
simplexes have K constrained dimensions, etc.)

- Bob
